A fix release. There are no API changes, so it is safe to upgrade.

## Fixes

- **Dark mode with remembered and shipped layouts.** A layout recorded on a light page no longer shows a white card on a dark page, or the other way round. If the page's tone is different from when the layout was recorded, autobones draws a neutral outline in the bone color instead of the recorded colors. The tone is judged from the page's real backgrounds, so it follows your own theme switch and not only the operating system setting. Layout files recorded before this release still work and are drawn as recorded.
- **Pages with hundreds of skeletons no longer freeze when resized.** A separate skeleton around each card used to redraw one at a time, and each one waited for the previous one's changes to settle. A resize with 500 cards froze the page for over two seconds. All skeletons now redraw together in a single frame: that same resize takes about 0.3 seconds. Bones that did not move are no longer rebuilt, and a skeleton that cannot be measured no longer stops the others.

## Docs

- A "Long lists" guide in the README, with measured numbers and advice for very long lists (the shimmer animation itself costs frames above roughly 500 cards, so use `animation="none"` or render fewer placeholder cards).
- A "Light and dark" note for shipped layouts.
- The React section says which versions are supported: 17, 18 and 19.
- An npm badge and a working "Live demo" link on the package page.

## Tested

- Every change now runs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (Safari's engine), and the React adapter runs on React 17, 18 and 19.
- The suite has 235 tests.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install autobones@latest
```

## Known limits

- The shimmer animation costs frames on lists of several hundred cards or more (see "Long lists" in the README).
- A layout is stored once per width, not once per theme, so a visitor in the other theme sees a neutral outline for the card rather than your exact dark or light card.
- The Vue and Svelte adapters are tested through render functions and a direct call to the action. Single-file components and the Svelte compiler are not covered yet.
- With server-side rendering, the real content shows briefly before the skeleton takes over on hydration.
